name: Cuba
people: Where Cubans and Co-designers design the nation they want to live in.
codesigner: Everyone who shares a vision, a voice or an enterprise here becomes a Co-designer of Perfect Cuba: one of a community of selfless people, at home and abroad, building a nation where every citizen has a decent life.

paras: Your farmland covers six tenths of your land, nine in ten of your young people complete lower secondary school, and almost every home has drinking water. Yet by the strict international measure, 54.1% of you lack safely managed sanitation. Let the next investment in Cuba reach the pipes and treatment that every home needs.

mandates.terms: For the Government of Cuba, its development partners and investors. Scope and fees are agreed in writing before any work begins.

capita.pc_text: The yearly cost, per person, of lifting everyone above the Living Line in all seven basic living standards, set with Cuba in its own prices.
capita.price_text: Perfect Capita times the population: the national bill, each year.
capita.est: Perfect Nations estimate, to be confirmed with Cuba. Figures marked dated rest on surveys more than five years old; lenient measures are marked as such.
capita.measures: Strict measures. Food: share not moderately or severely food insecure (FAO). Water: safely managed drinking water where measured; where it is not, basic water, marked as such. Shelter: the lower of safely managed sanitation and the share outside urban slums. Energy: the lower of electricity per person against 1,000 kWh and clean cooking; where electricity per person is not published, clean cooking. Education: the lower of children reading by the end of primary school and lower-secondary completion. Health: WHO service coverage index. Livelihood: share above the stricter of the national poverty line and the World Bank line for the nation’s income group (US$8.30 a day for high-income nations). Each figure links to its source. For Cuba, the delivery test (12 November 2026): where the nation’s own agencies publish how much of a service reaches people, the lower figure counts. Water: the share whose piped supply is not cut (INRH). Energy: the share of evening peak demand the grid can serve (Unión Eléctrica). Health: the share of the basic list of medicines available (President of Cuba).

voices.local: We are looking for the people with real stories from Cuba: the leaders who built something that works, and the keepers of local knowledge who know how their communities live, cope and thrive.

close_lead: Share your vision, suggest a guest, or write to us. Every message receives a personal reply.
sources: World Bank, World Development Indicators (API), accessed 10 November 2026: population and ages 0 to 14, 2025; land area and agricultural and forest land; renewable fresh water per person, 2022; natural resource, oil, gas and mineral rents, 2021; renewable electricity output, 2021; tourism receipts; personal remittances; electricity access and clean cooking.

The seven standards: FAO food insecurity, WHO/UNICEF JMP water and sanitation, UN-Habitat urban slums, World Bank clean cooking, learning poverty and lower-secondary completion, and poverty headcounts (all via the World Bank); WHO UHC service coverage index, 2023.
IMF, World Economic Outlook, October 2026 (DataMapper, accessed 10 November 2026): general government gross debt, 2025, and real GDP growth projected for 2026.

National sources, read 12 November 2026: ONEI population with effective residence, 31 December 2025 (Prensa Latina, 21 July 2026); INRH, people with piped water cut, 3 November 2026 (Cubadebate); Unión Eléctrica, daily note of 10 November 2026 (Granma); President of Cuba, speech of 8 August 2026; WFP, Cuba country strategic plan 2026 to 2030 (May 2026).
